absent: Full layouts of backing_aio, backing_file_ctx, kiocb, iov_iter, file, inode, dentry, pipe_inode_info, pipe_buffer and vm_area_struct beyond members named in fragments.
Async backing completion path including workqueue setup, queueing routine, reference release, cleanup, and end_write and accessed callback contracts and timing.
Privilege and security details including ownership drop rules, security hook verdicts, attribute change mechanics, idmap translation, and numeric values of ATTR, SB and S flags.
Range verification bounds, maximum transfer constant, mode and flag numerics for FMODE, IOCB, O_DIRECT and rwf_t, and freeze accounting depth rules.
Pipe ring management including sizing, locking, wakeups, full and empty handling, and default buffer operation behavior.
Filesystem hook contracts for vectored read and write and splice read and write, including position update, short transfer and DAX detection rules.
Mapping path details including area file replacement, backing security checks, compatibility wrapper, mappability of diverse filesystems, and failure rollback.
Bad-inode lifecycle including hash handling, timestamp initialization, reference counting, lock ordering, and callers of poisoning and failure helpers.
ELF loading beyond stack setup including binary parsing, page size and task size values, auxiliary vector sizing and numerics, and the remainder of table creation.
Boot ordering and concurrency for the async cache creation, slab alignment guarantees, and behavior under memory pressure beyond immediate errors.

findings.text: Backing write wrapper is the public entry for writing through a backing handle. Successful transfers run under caller-supplied credentials and honor an optional completion callback. Empty payloads succeed immediately. Handles lacking the backing marker warn once and fail as I/O error. Direct mode demands direct capability on the backing handle, otherwise an invalid-argument failure results, and privilege bits are stripped from the original user handle before movement. Capability names involved are FMODE_CAN_ODIRECT alongside FMODE_BACKING with IOCB_DIRECT.

Backing write dispatch offers two completion contracts. Synchronous callers receive inline results with flags translated to generic semantics and an optional finish hook observing the outcome. Asynchronous callers use an auxiliary record with dual-reference accounting, a cloned control block carrying caller flags and a queueing completion routine, workqueue readiness, and submission through the async vector helper. One reference is released immediately after submission; outcomes other than queued trigger synchronous cleanup, while allocation or readiness failures propagate directly without invoking the finish hook. Status EIOCBQUEUED distinguishes queued completion while ENOMEM signals allocation failure.

Vectored async write helper emits a modify notification for positive transfers. Entry requires vector support, write permission and write capability, each absence failing distinctly. Empty iterators succeed with zero without filesystem contact. Delegation occurs only after range validation, bracketed by accounting start and end, with the end marker skipped when completion is queued. Mode bits of interest are FMODE_CAN_WRITE with FMODE_WRITE. Position state is tracked in ki_pos.

Synchronous vectored write helper emits a modify notification on positive transfers and updates the caller position through delegation. Hook presence alongside capability and permission gates entry, with empty iterators short-circuiting to zero. Range validation gates freeze acquisition and filesystem delegation, with freeze release always pairing acquisition. Modes of interest are FMODE_CAN_WRITE with FMODE_WRITE.

Write accounting is strictly paired on all examined paths. Freeze release always matches a preceding freeze acquisition for synchronous vector writes and backing splice writes, including failure exits after acquisition. Async accounting end matches start except when completion is queued for later. Pairing scopes cover filesystem delegation and, for backing splice, execute under caller credentials.

Freeze protection is a no-op for non-regular files and engages superblock accounting only for regular ones. The test consults the mode of the inode bound to the handle. Start and end helpers are symmetric. Regular test uses S_ISREG.

Privilege stripping may opportunistically mark an inode no-security when set-id bits are absent and the superblock opts out. Stripping is skipped entirely for no-security inodes and non-regular modes. A nonzero kill mask forces non-blocking callers to fail fast with a retry status rather than sleep, while blocking callers apply a forced attribute change through the generic change path. The mask combines idmap-aware ownership rules with a security hook verdict, whose negative outcome propagates immediately. Top-level wrapper delegates with zero extra flags. Markers include SB_NOSEC with S_NOSEC and ATTR_FORCE alongside ATTR_KILL_PRIV plus IOCB_NOWAIT.

Dentry derivation from an open handle has no failure modes and performs no locking; it returns the path component while asserting cached consistency via a one-time warning. Mount identity mapping derives from the mount component of the same path, also infallible.

Backing splice read delegates data movement to the generic splice path under caller-supplied credentials using the control block position. An optional accessed hook observes the original user file afterwards regardless of outcome. Handles lacking the backing marker warn once and fail as I/O error without delegating. Marker is FMODE_BACKING.

Generic splice read dispatches to the filesystem hook except for direct or DAX-backed handles, which use a copy-based staging fallback. Missing filesystem support emits a rate-limited diagnostic naming the operation and fails as invalid argument. Requests are capped by free pipe capacity converted to bytes and by a global maximum bound, with zero length succeeding immediately. Handles lacking read permission fail with a bad-descriptor status, and range validation gates all dispatch. Caps involve MAX_RW_COUNT with O_DIRECT plus FMODE_READ.

Out-of-memory failures at either allocation step release partial storage. Bulk page allocation may yield fewer pages than requested, shrinking the transfer to what was obtained. Descriptor and page-pointer storage is allocated together and zeroed. Staging never exceeds free pipe slots converted to bytes and rounded up to whole pages.

A retry status is reported instead of a fault status from the staging read, matching splice caller expectations. Caller position advances to the control block position only on positive transfers; non-positive outcomes leave it unchanged. Codes EAGAIN with EFAULT are the translated pair.

Descriptor storage is always freed before return. Touched pages are inserted at the pipe head with default operations, zero offset and lengths covering remaining bytes, advancing the head per page. Untouched trailing pages are released. Page count retained derives from rounding the transfer count up to whole pages. Insertion operations are default_pipe_buf_ops.

Pipe addressing is pure arithmetic without locking. Occupancy is head minus tail in index type. Usage equals occupancy. Slot lookup masks by ring size minus one. Head accessor resolves the current head slot.

Backing splice write invokes an optional finish hook with the outcome whenever configured, even on failure. Filesystem delegation runs under caller credentials with freeze protection and control block position. Privileges are stripped from the originating file beforehand. Required preconditions are the backing marker and presence of the filesystem splice hook, each absence failing distinctly.

Backing mmap reports success from generic mapping after security approval and file substitution. An optional accessed hook observes the original user file after setup. Security validation for the backing mapping runs under caller credentials and gates any mapping work. Preconditions are the backing marker and filesystem mappability, each violation failing distinctly, with the area file replaced by the backing file before validation.

Mapping dispatch prefers the prepare variant through a compatibility wrapper and otherwise invokes the legacy hook directly. Dual hook presence warns once and counts as unmappable, as does absence of both. Hooks are mmap_prepare with mmap.

Boot-time initializer establishes a dedicated slab cache for async backing records. Success yields zero. Creation failure propagates out-of-memory with no cache left behind. Alignment uses SLAB_HWCACHE_ALIGN; failure status is ENOMEM.

Poisoned tables enforce a fail-closed contract for unusable inodes. Pointer-returning operations encode an I/O error in the returned pointer; all other operations return that error directly. Coverage spans file open, time updates, content mapping queries, extended attributes, attributes, permissions, linking, lookup and directory mutation. The file table exposes only an open entry while the inode table wires every supported operation to a failing stub. Failure status is EIO.

Poisoning leaves an inode with refreshed timestamps and failing operation tables, unhashed. Extended-attribute capability is cleared while other operation flags are preserved. Cleared flag is IOP_XATTR; mode becomes S_IFREG; the file table installed is bad_file_ops with inode table bad_inode_ops.
Failed acquisition leaves no usable inode. Postconditions are release of the acquisition reference, observable completion of creation for waiters, and a poisoned operation set.

New-inode publication wakes waiters on the creation bit after clearing both new and creating states under the inode spinlock. A write barrier separates the state clear from the wakeup to pair with hash acquisition. Lockdep annotation for directory mutexes precedes the locked section. The holder must hold no other conflicting inode state; a warning fires if the new state was already absent.

Directory mutex rekeying applies only to directory inodes whose semaphore still carries the generic filesystem class. Matching entries receive a fresh semaphore and the directory-specific class. Non-directories and already-customized directories are untouched and no locking is taken by the helper itself.

Compatibility and dump defaults are zero-valued with null platform and dump hooks. ELF_COMPAT is zero and ELF_CORE_EFLAGS is zero. Base platform pointer ELF_BASE_PLATFORM is null and dump hook elf_core_dump is null. Type aliases map user_long_t to long and user_siginfo_t to siginfo_t. FDPIC check elf_check_fdpic is constantly false.

Page alignment derives from a minimum granularity with two configuration variants. One variant ties granularity to the base page size; the other ties it to the executable page size. Start rounds an address down by masking off low bits, offset extracts those low bits, and aligned end rounds up by adding granularity minus one before masking. Granularity symbol is ELF_MIN_ALIGN with helpers ELF_PAGEALIGN plus ELF_PAGEOFFSET and ELF_PAGESTART.

Tail padding clears bytes from an address up to the next granularity boundary and reports a fault status if user clearing fails; already-aligned addresses succeed trivially. Address validity treats any value at or above the task size as bad. Bound symbol is BAD_ADDR with task limit TASK_SIZE.

ELF handler table binds this module to the ELF loader with an optional dump hook and a minimum dump granularity when dumps are configured. Core flag save and restore are no-ops unless the architecture enables dedicated core flag storage, in which case they exchange a saved field in the memory descriptor. Table is elf_format with granularity ELF_EXEC_PAGESIZE.

Initial stack construction has ascending and descending configuration variants. One variant grows the pointer backward by item count and allocates by retreating; the other grows forward and allocates by advancing after returning the old pointer. Both round the resulting pointer to sixteen bytes. Variants are STACK_ALLOC with STACK_ROUND plus STACK_ADD, each with ascending and descending forms.

Process stack setup publishes platform strings, randomness and an auxiliary vector for the new image. Random seeding uses sixteen bytes copied to the stack. Optional platform and base-platform strings are copied when present. The vector records credentials-derived identifiers, security state, entry and base addresses, header location and counts, timing and paging parameters, hardware capabilities and the random address, followed by architecture extras. Stack alignment is applied before any copying. Copy failures to user memory abort with a fault status. Helper is NEW_AUX_ENT.

Failure handling favors explicit propagation over retry except where noted. Allocation exhaustion, missing hooks, permission absences and backing violations each yield distinct errors without partial side effects beyond warnings or diagnostics. Non-blocking privilege stripping fails fast rather than sleeping. Faults during staging reads surface as retryable for splice callers. One-time warnings flag programming errors such as missing backing markers, inconsistent dentry state, absent new state, or dual mapping hooks.
Modify notifications for successful writes collapse to a file-level modify event. Positive transfer counts trigger exactly one such event; zero or negative outcomes trigger none.
